caption:
Everyone’s posting their Euro summer… but can you believe this isn’t Europe?  It’s actually just 2 hours from Toronto, Canada 🤭🇨🇦 

We recently took @citycruisescanada 1-hour sightseeing cruise through the 1000 Islands, and it reminded us how many beautiful places we have right here in Ontario. 

If you’re looking for an easy summer getaway, add this to your bucket list ☀️ #citycruisespartner 

Here’s how we’d spend the day: 
🚢 Choose from a 1-hour, 3-hour, or 5-hour sightseeing cruise (the 5 hour cruise includes a stop at Boldt Castle but don’t forget your passport!)
🏰 Cruise past stunning waterfront mansions, castles, and tiny islands, it’s the perfect place to gather dream home inspiration!!!
✨ You’ll also see the World’s Shortest International Bridge connecting Canada and the U.S. it’s only about 10 feet (3m) long and ridiculously cute.
🍔 After your cruise, grab lunch at Dockside Restaurant and order their award-winning 1000 Islands Burger. Yup the dressing is in the burger 👅
🍦Finish the day with an ice cream from The Ice Cream Stop and a stroll along Gananoque’s waterfront.

caption:
🇪🇸 ULTIMATE 5 DAY MALLORCA ITINERARY ↓

This summer, @aircanada is launching new flights to Mallorca, making it one of the easiest Mediterranean islands to reach from North America!

Here’s how to spend five incredible days on the island:

DAY 1 - ARRIVAL & PALMA
✈️ Fly into Palma with @aircanada
⛪ Visit the Cathedral of Santa Maria
🍦 Wander the old streets and grab gelato

DAY 2 - MOUNTAIN VILLAGES
🏡 Wander the stone streets, little shops, and viewpoints
🌄 Spend the afternoon in Deià
🍹 Stay for sunset drinks if you can

DAYS 3/4 - BEACHES
🏖️ Beach hop between Cala des Moro, Cala Llombards, Cala Ferrera, and Cala Mendia
🐟 Visit Cala Figuera and walk around the traditional fishing port
🍽️ Have lunch at Bon Bar in Cala Figuera
🚤 Take a boat trip along the Santanyí coast
🍽️ For dinner, check out Qanat at Finca Treurer or Castillo del Bosque
🏨 Stay at Belle Son Mas Luxury

DAY 5 - CUEVAS DEL DRACH
🕯️ Visit Cuevas del Drach, a super impressive underground cave system with one of the largest underground lakes in the world
🧂 Stop by Flor de Sal at Salinas d’Es Trenc
🌆 If you have extra time, head back to Palma for one final walk through the old town

So if Mallorca is on your bucket list, save this reel, check the caption for all our recommendations, and tag someone who needs to see this.

If you find yourself in Sölden, Austria 🇦🇹 you need to add this place to your bucket-list!

caption:
$35 for a carton of orange juice 🤯

Ever wondered what life is really like in Canada’s Arctic? Even in late summer it was straight up freezing, around five degrees. Our first stop was the grocery store, where a jug of juice costs $35 and the most northern KFC in the world was closed. That’s when it really hit us how remote this place is.

Inuit communities here rely on country food, wild local meals that have sustained them for thousands of years. Arctic char, muskox soup, beluga, narwhal, even polar bear. Every bite carries a story of survival, culture, and tradition. 🤍

We also witnessed traditions that have been passed down for generations. A qulliq oil lamp being lit, haunting throat singing, and a powerful Inuit drum dance. These aren’t performances. They are a way of life, a living connection to the land, and a reminder of incredible resilience.

This is a side of Canada few people ever get to see. Remote, raw, and full of life. Something we will never forget. 🫶🏻

Thank you @seabourncruise for giving us this incredible experience

caption:
Come make pierogies with my Babcia and me!🇵🇱

She doesn’t speak English (only Polish) but she’s so funny that I had to leave her comments in! 

Her pierogi’s are THE BEST, so here’s her recipe for Polish/Ruthenian (cheese & potatoe filled) pierogi. 

✨WHAT YOULL NEED✨

• 500g of all-purpose flour
• 1.5 lbs of potatoes
• 2 onions 
• 400g of Twarog cheese (I bought MC diary pressed cottage cheese from Walmart)
• half a stick of butter 
• cooking oil 
• 1 egg
• salt and pepper to taste 
•paprika (I like to use a lot, but up to your preference) 
• 150 ml of warm water 

✨METHOD✨

1. Peel and boil potatoes. You want to be sure the potatoes are extra extra cooked and easy to smash. Strain and save the boiled potatoe water for later. 
2. While the potatoes are boiling, chop the onion. Get a good cry in 😅
3. Put all the butter on the pan and sizzle the onion. Don’t forget to season with salt and generously with the paprika.
4. In a mixing bowl, add the flour, and slowly pour in the warm water while mixing. Add in some cooking oil (I used olive) and add in 1 egg yolk. Mix  and knead the dough - I find using your hands is best for this. Set aside. 
5. You’re halfway done so treat yourself to a cold Polish beer 😅🍺
6.  Now time for the filing: Using a hardcore potato masher (I got mine off of Amazon I’ll link it in my recipe stories), add half the boiled potatoes and mash them through. Next add the cheese, and finish with the rest of the potatoes. 
7. Add 3/4 of the sautéed onion to the filling, add salt pepper and paprika (be generous and taste test along the way) and mix together using your hands. 
8. Roll the dough out so it’s flat, and using a cup, cut out circles. You’ll fill these circles with the filing to make little pierogies. I add about 2 spoons of filling per pieróg.
9. Reheat the boiled water from the potatoes, add in your pierogies for about 5mins until they float.
10. Serve with the remaining sautéed onion and enjoy!!!☺️

We used our @hexclad pans and love them!
